title: Compound & double-angle formulae
examples: How do I use these formulas when I see sin(x+y)?
Can you show me another example for the cosine double angle formula?
What is the easiest form of the double angle formula for cosine?

explain.say: Today we learn some useful angle formulas. We start with the sine of a sum or difference. The formula for sine of A plus B is sin A cos B plus cos A sin B.

draw.text: sin(A+B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B

explain.say: Next, let us look at the sine of A minus B. This one is sin A cos B minus cos A sin B. Remember to keep the signs correct.

items: sin(A+B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B
sin(A-B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B

draw.text: sin(A-B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B

explain.say: Now we look at double angles for cosine. One form is cos two A equals cos squared A minus sin squared A. This is always true.
Another useful form for cosine is cos two A equals two cos squared A minus one. This form is helpful when you know the cosine value. Let us try that.

faq.q: When should I use the compound angle formulas?
faq.a: You use them when you see an angle that is the sum or difference of two known angles. For example, if you see sin(x + 30 degrees), you can break it down.
asks: What are compound angle identities for sine?

faq.q: Are there different forms for cos two A?
faq.a: Yes, there are three main forms for cosine double angle. They are cos squared A minus sin squared A, two cos squared A minus one, and one minus two sin squared A.
asks: Which cos(2A) formula should I use?
Show me all the double angle formulas for cosine.

faq.q: Can I use these formulas for any angle?
faq.a: These formulas work for any real number angle measurement. You must make sure your calculator is in the correct degree or radian mode.
asks: Do these formulas only work for degrees?

faq.q: What is the difference between A and B in these formulas?
faq.a: A and B represent any two angles you are working with. You can substitute any values for A and B into the identity.
asks: What do A and B stand for?
Can A and B be the same angle?

faq.q: If I know sin A, can I find cos(2A)?
faq.a: Yes, if you know sin A, you can use the form cos two A equals one minus two sin squared A. This lets you solve it using only sine.
asks: What if I only have sine values?
How do I find cos(2A) from sin A?

facts: The formula sin(A+B) is sin A cos B plus cos A sin B.
The formula sin(A-B) is sin A cos B minus cos A sin B.
One form for cosine double angle is cos two A equals cos squared A minus sin squared A.
Another useful form is cos two A equals two cos squared A minus one.

quiz.say: If sin A equals one half and cos B equals one half, what is sin(A+B)?
quiz.why: You correctly applied the formula sin A cos B plus cos A sin B.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you added the two given values together.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you incorrectly subtracted the two given values.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you multiplied the two given values together.

quiz.say: If cos A equals one half, what is the value of cos two A using the form two cos squared A minus one?
quiz.why: Substituting one half for cos A gives two times one half squared minus one, which is negative one.

wrong.1: This mistake happens because you thought the formula was simply cos A minus one.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you forgot to square the value of cos A first.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you only used the value of cos A once.

quiz.say: Which expression is equal to sin A cos B minus cos A sin B?
quiz.why: This pattern directly matches the identity for the sine of a difference.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the sign between the terms is subtraction, not addition.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the formula requires multiplying the terms together, not squaring them separately.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the pattern matches the sine difference, not the cosine sum.
